# Real-Time Inventory Sync System  

A robust solution for synchronizing inventory across distributed systems, leveraging Apache Kafka for event streaming and cloud-native storage for persistent data. Designed to ensure zero latency updates, this system resolves common bottlenecks in e-commerce platforms by eliminating manual reconciliation and enabling real-time visibility across all touchpoints.

## Getting Started / Installation  
To operationalize the system, first deploy a Kafka cluster and configure a cloud storage backend (e.g., S3-compatible object storage). Install the core components via npm:  
```bash  
npm install  
```  
Initialize the Kafka producers and consumers with environment variables pointing to your storage endpoint. Ensure all nodes are synchronized with a shared time source to avoid drift in event timestamps.  

## Tech Stack  
- Apache Kafka (for real-time event streaming)  
- Cloud storage (e.g., S3, Google Cloud Storage)  
- JSON-based messaging protocol  
- Lightweight, stateless microservices for scalability  

## Architecture / Design  
The system operates as a distributed event-driven pipeline. Producers publish inventory changes to Kafka topics, which are consumed by sync workers. These workers apply updates to the cloud storage backend, ensuring atomic writes and version control. A publish-subscribe model allows multiple downstream systems (e.g., POS, marketplaces) to subscribe to inventory events without coupling. The architecture prioritizes fault tolerance by replicating Kafka partitions and using idempotent writes to prevent duplicate updates.  

## Usage / Examples  
To publish an inventory update:  
```bash  
node producer.js --item-id 123 --quantity 50 --action update  
```  
Consumers automatically apply the change to the storage backend. For querying, use the built-in API to fetch current stock levels, ensuring all reads reflect the latest state. This setup prevents overselling by enforcing real-time validation across all access points.  

## Testing  
Validate the system through stress testing with synthetic load, ensuring sub-100ms latency for 99.9% of events. Perform data integrity checks by comparing Kafka offsets with storage backend records. Simulate network partitions to verify fallback mechanisms and confirm that all updates are eventually reconciled.
